# Model Merging {#sec-model-merging}

```{r}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
mdl_key_style <- doc_manifest()$id_field == "mdl_key"
```

A taxon may have distribution data in several source datasets. Merging combines them into **one surface per taxon**, applying the taxon's governing extinction risk and constraining the result to where experts say the species actually occurs.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Interactive walkthrough

The [Scoring Walkthrough](scoring-walkthrough.qmd) animates this — maximum merge, range masking and the regulatory floors, step by step from input rasters.
:::

## The rule, in one place

The merge rules are **`msens::merge_sql()`**, **`msens::turtle_sql()`** and **`msens::dps_sql()`** — SQL held in the package rather than inside a notebook. The merge notebook executes them and the unit tests assert them against synthetic fixtures, one per taxon category, so the pipeline and its tests cannot drift apart. Changing a rule in a way that breaks a documented case fails the tests.

## The sequence, end to end {#sec-merge-sequence}

Each merged model is the result of a fixed sequence of processes, each with a named output. The
diagram shows every process a taxon can pass through and the artifact each one writes; the table
after it says which rule a taxon takes and what its cell value, its risk layer and its score are
under that rule. Steps marked *v11 option* are method flags under review for v11 and are **off** in
every released version, where the pipeline reproduces the earlier rule exactly.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-merge-sequence
%%| fig-cap: "Processes (boxes), their outputs (cylinders) and the order they run in, from the ingested models to the zone scores. Dashed boxes are v11 options, off in every release so far."
%%| fig-width: 7
flowchart TD
  I["1 Ingest<br>one notebook per source dataset<br>onto the 0.05 degree grid"] --> D[("dist/dataset={ds}<br>model, cell, val<br>+ model_{ds}.csv")]
  D --> X["2 Crosswalk and governing risk (merge_models_prep)<br>models to WoRMS / BirdLife taxa; er_score = the US ESA<br>status (higher of NMFS / FWS) over the IUCN category,<br>MMPA / MBTA floors; datasets the run does not use are<br>dropped here (AquaX unless AX_SUPERSEDE, og, density)"]
  X --> TM[("taxon, taxon_model, listing<br>(merge.duckdb)")]
  TM --> S["3 Supersession on the merge input<br>AquaX replaces AquaMaps inside the AquaX mask (v9;<br>moot in v10 and v11, which run without AquaX)"]

  S --> P[("mc_parts<br>partitioned merge input")]
  S2 -.-> P
  P --> R{"4 Which rule?"}
  R -->|"sea turtle"| RT["turtle_sql (v4b): value = max(1, round(risk_c x suit / 100)),<br>suit = 1 where no model covers the cell;<br>critical habitat by max; risk inside the value"]
  R -.->|"sea turtle, TURTLE_RULE=dps<br>(v11 option)"| RT2["dps_sql: value = suitability, risk_c beside it;<br>critical habitat joins the risk footprint"]
  R -->|"NMFS DPS-listed species (v9)"| RD["dps_sql: value = suitability masked to the<br>risk footprint, the cell's risk where no model<br>covers it; per-cell risk beside the value"]
  R -.->|"density taxon (v11 option)"| RE["dps_sql with the governing er_score<br>as the floor under the per-cell risk"]

  RT --> G
  RT2 -.-> G
  RD --> G
  RE -.-> G
  RM --> G
  G["5 Zone edits (v11 options, on the value surfaces only)<br>occurrence gate: no OBIS record in an ecoregion under adequate<br>effort, the species' cells there are dropped; encounter weight:<br>value x w, w = min(1, its record rate there / its rate elsewhere);<br>critical habitat exempt; the per-cell risk is never adjusted"]
  G --> O1[("dist_merged_global<br>whole-range surface<br>(what the Atlas draws)")]
  G --> O2[("dist_merged<br>US-trimmed scoring surface")]
  RD --> O3[("dist_merged_er<br>per-cell risk beside the value<br>(cell-mode taxa)")]
  RE -.-> O3
  RT2 -.-> O3
  O2 --> MT["6 merge_taxon, score_zones<br>validity, is_marine, category;<br>model_cell / model_cell_er copied in;<br>er_mode assigned: taxon | premultiplied | cell"]
  O3 --> MT
  MT --> SC["7 Cell scoring (score_cell_metrics)<br>extrisk = sum over species of risk x value / 100;<br>risk = er_score (taxon) | the cell's (cell)<br>| 100, already inside the value (premultiplied)"]
  SC --> O4[("cell_metric<br>extrisk_{category}")]
  O4 --> Z8["8a v8 zone scores<br>rescaled within the ecoregion,<br>coverage-weighted to the zone"]
  MT --> Z10["8b v10 share scores<br>each species' value / its global total,<br>risk-weighted, kappa = 5 % floor,<br>equal-weight composite"]
  O1 --> TD[("taxon_denom<br>each species' global total: the global surface,<br>or AquaMaps outside the US + model_cell inside it<br>for AquaMaps-only taxa, or a curated fallback")]
  TD --> Z10
  Z8 --> O5[("zone_metric, zone_taxon")]

  style S2 stroke-dasharray: 4 3
  style RT2 stroke-dasharray: 4 3
  style RE stroke-dasharray: 4 3
  style G stroke-dasharray: 4 3
```

Order matters in three places. Supersession (3) runs **before** any rule, so a rule never sees a
superseded cell. The range mask is part of each rule (4), not a later pass: a suitability model's
cells beyond the expert range never enter either surface. And the zone edits (5) wrap each rule's
output as it is written, after the rule has valued the cells, so they can remove or weight cells
without changing what the rule computed, and they never touch the per-cell risk layer.

### Which rule a taxon takes

| taxon | inputs | merged value in a cell | risk layer | `er_mode` | cell score (@eq-cell-score and its two exceptions) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AquaMaps only, no expert range anywhere (most scored taxa) | AquaMaps (AquaX where it superseded, v9) | each model's suitability, raw footprint, on the US surface only (a taxon with several AquaMaps models keeps every model's cell) | the scalar `er_score` | `taxon` | `er_score x suit / 100` |
| expert range and AquaMaps | range map(s) + AquaMaps / AquaX | `max(er_score, suit)` on range cells; suitability beyond the range masked away (v11 option, cell basis: `suit` where a model covers the cell, the `RANGE_FILL` value where none does) | the scalar `er_score` | `taxon` | `er_score x max(er_score, suit) / 100` (cell basis: `er_score x suit / 100`) |
| expert range only (most of them birds) | IUCN / BirdLife / FWS range | `er_score` on every range cell | the scalar `er_score` | `taxon` | `er_score x er_score / 100` |
| sea turtle | SWOT + DPS risk surface, AquaMaps / AquaX (or `og`, v11 option), critical habitat | `max(1, round(risk_c x suit / 100))`, suit = 1 where no model covers the cell, critical habitat by max | inside the value | `premultiplied` | the value itself (weight 100 by `er_mode`) |
| NMFS DPS-listed species (v9) | `dps_nmfs` per-cell risk, AquaX / AquaMaps | suitability where a model covers the cell, the cell's risk where none does | per-cell `er_c` beside the value | `cell` | `er_c x value / 100`, so `er_c x er_c / 100` where no model covers the cell |
| density taxon (v11 option) | survey density inside its domain, AquaMaps outside, range maps | as the DPS rule, with the governing `er_score` as a floor under the per-cell risk | per-cell `er_c` (at least `er_score`) | `cell` | as the DPS rule |
| sea turtle under `TURTLE_RULE=dps` (v11 option) | as above | as the DPS rule, critical habitat joining the risk footprint | per-cell `er_c` | `cell` | as the DPS rule |

### Where the risk enters, and how many times

The table makes one property of the released rule explicit. For a taxon with an expert range the
governing `er_score` is used **twice**: once at merge time, as the floor under every range cell
(@eq-merge-range), and again at scoring, as the multiplier (@eq-cell-score). A range cell no
suitability model covers therefore scores `er_score^2 / 100` (25 for a score of 50), and wherever the
suitability is below the governing score the risk, not the model, shapes the distribution. Only
where suitability exceeds the score does the cell carry the risk-weighted suitability a reader
might expect. AquaMaps-only taxa are single-counted (the first row), and so are the sea turtles under
their own rule (a cell no model covers takes suitability 1, and the weight is 100). The DPS-listed
species, and the v11 taxa that share their rule, are single-counted wherever a suitability model
covers the cell; a footprint cell no model covers is valued at its risk and so scores `er_c^2 / 100`,
like a range cell. This has been the rule since v4; it is stated here so that the two counts are not
mistaken for one.

The v10 share score (@sec-scoring, the share section) divides each species' cell value by the
species' own total built from the same merged values, so for a range-only taxon the constant risk
level cancels and the risk enters the share once, as the weight. What survives there is the
**shape**: cells no model covers, and cells whose suitability is below the governing score, are
raised to the score relative to the modelled cells. Under the pooled denominator the level does not
cancel.

A v11 option, `SHARE_BASIS = cell`, values a range cell by its suitability alone wherever a model
covers it, for every taxon, and `RANGE_FILL` decides a cell no model covers: the governing score
(`er`, which still counts the risk twice there), presence, 100 (`presence`, which counts it once),
or the mean of the species' own modelled footprint cells (`mean`: for a surveyed species the
survey's mean value over its domain, and presence for a species with no model at all). The same
fill applies to the DPS rule and the taxa that share it. The v11 method set uses the cell basis
with the mean fill; both flags are off in every release so far, where the pipeline reproduces the
earlier rule exactly.

## Pipeline

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-merge-pipeline
%%| fig-cap: "Merging one taxon's source models into a single surface."
%%| fig-width: 6
flowchart TD
  A["Gather this taxon's models<br>across all source datasets"] --> T{"Sea turtle?"}
  T -->|Yes| M["Multiply DPS extinction-risk<br>surface by suitability"]
  T -->|No| P{"NMFS DPS-listed<br>species?"}
  P -->|Yes| Q["Suitability masked to the<br>extinction-risk footprint;<br>per-cell risk kept beside it"]
  P -->|No| B{"Has an expert range<br>anywhere in the world?"}
  Q --> F
  B -->|Yes| C["Range footprint valued at<br>max(governing er_score,<br>AquaMaps at those cells)"]
  B -->|No| D["Raw AquaMaps footprint<br>(no expert range to constrain it)"]
  M --> E["Critical habitat<br>overrides with a max"]
  C --> F["Persist to the<br>merged surface"]
  D --> F
  E --> F
```

### Step 1 — gather the taxon's models

Every model resolving to the same taxon is collected: an AquaMaps suitability surface, any regulatory habitat or range designation (NMFS, FWS), a BirdLife or IUCN range map, and for sea turtles a SWOT+DPS range.

### Step 2 — the expert range constrains AquaMaps

This is the heart of the merge, and it is not a plain maximum.

Where a taxon **has an expert range**, the merged surface is the **range footprint**, valued at the maximum of the taxon's governing `er_score` and the AquaMaps value *at those cells*:

$$
v_{c} = \max\!\big(\text{er\_score},\; v_{am,c}\big) \qquad c \in \text{range}
$$ {#eq-merge-range}

AquaMaps values **beyond** the range are masked away. An environmental-envelope model will happily predict suitable habitat far outside where a species is known to occur; the expert range is what stops that prediction becoming an assertion of presence.

Where a taxon has **no expert range anywhere**, there is nothing to constrain it against, so its raw AquaMaps footprint is kept as-is.

::: {.callout-important}
## "Has a range" is a **global** question, not a local one

Whether a taxon counts as range-constrained is decided on its range **anywhere in the world**, not on whether that range reaches the study area.

That distinction is the entire mechanism for excluding species whose expert range lies wholly outside US waters. Such a species has an expert range, so it takes the range-constrained path; its range ∩ US is empty, so it contributes **no US cells**. Deciding instead on "has a range *in the US*" would push those same species onto the unconstrained AquaMaps path and re-admit roughly **750** of them — river dolphins such as *Sotalia guianensis* among them — on the strength of edge-of-range model artifacts that expert assessment places nowhere near the US.

This was a v6 fix, lost in the v8 rewrite and since restored. It is now a named regression test.
:::

### Step 3 — two surfaces, not one

```{r}
#| label: two-surfaces
#| output: asis

if (mdl_key_style) {
  cat(
"Since v8 the merge emits **two** surfaces from the same rules, because they answer different
questions:

- a **global** surface — the taxon's whole range footprint under the same rule and the same range
  mask (AquaMaps beyond the expert range is masked away here too), which is what the species maps
  draw; AquaMaps-only taxa are drawn from their AquaMaps model directly;
- a **US scoring** surface — the range-constrained, US-clipped result described above, which is
  what the scores are computed from.

Earlier releases produced only the second, so a species map showed the analysis extent rather
than the species. Keeping both means the picture is not silently trimmed to the study area.\n\n",
sep = "")
}
```

### Step 4 — sea turtles multiply instead of taking a maximum

For the six sea turtle species, extinction risk **varies across the range**: NOAA Fisheries lists Distinct Population Segments separately, so the same species can be Endangered in one region and Threatened in another. A single scalar weight cannot express that.

So the turtle merge multiplies the DPS extinction-risk surface by the suitability surface:

$$
v_{c} = \max\!\Big(1,\; \mathrm{round}\Big(\frac{v_{er,c} \times v_{suit,c}}{100}\Big)\Big)
$$ {#eq-merge-turtle}

Critical-habitat designations then override with a maximum, so a designated cell is never scored below its designation.

```{r}
#| output: asis
mth <- doc_manifest()$methods
if (!is.null(mth) && "turtle_suit_min" %in% mth$method_key) {
  g <- function(k) mth$value[mth$method_key == k]
  cat(glue::glue(
"**{doc_ver()} patches this rule**, without changing @eq-merge-turtle itself: the suitability term
\\(v_{{suit,c}}\\) is thresholded before the multiply. A suitability strictly below {g('turtle_suit_min')}
(AquaMaps' own core-habitat default, on its 0–100 scale) is treated as absent, and a range cell left
with none is **dropped** rather than filled at a nominal suitability of 1 — the fill v7 used, recorded
here as `turtle_fill = {g('turtle_fill')}`. Critical habitat still overrides by maximum, so a
designated cell is never lost to the threshold. Turning the threshold off (`turtle_suit_min = 0`)
reproduces v7's merged turtle models exactly. The threshold is AquaMaps' own convention rather than
a number tuned to the outcome. It leaves turtles in exactly one Alaska Program Area: the Gulf of
Alaska, 9,608 leatherback cells at suitability 0.50–0.58 off Southeast Alaska, where the region's
sparse occurrence records are [@hodgewing2000]. At 0.6 — the cutoff validated against surveys for
marine mammals [@kaschner2011] — no Alaska Program Area would retain turtles.\n\n"))
}
```

```{r}
#| output: asis
mth <- doc_manifest()$methods
if (!is.null(mth) && "turtle_record_rule" %in% mth$method_key) {
  g  <- function(k) if (k %in% mth$method_key) mth$value[mth$method_key == k][1] else NA_character_
  on <- function(k) identical(g(k), "on")
  cat(glue::glue(
"**{doc_ver()} edits the merged models after this rule, by ecoregion and by evidence**, and leaves
@eq-merge-turtle and the suitability surfaces exactly as v7 had them (no suitability threshold, the
range fill at 1 kept). Each cell belongs to the ecoregion covering most of it, and a species is
removed — the cell dropped, never set to zero — from an ecoregion listed in an evidence table of
species × ecoregion exclusions; every other cell keeps its v7 value, and a cell the species holds
under designated critical habitat is never removed."))
  cat("\n\n")
  if (on("turtle_record_rule")) cat(
"- **Turtle record rule** (`turtle_record_rule = on`): a sea-turtle species is excluded from an
  Alaska ecoregion where it has **never been recorded** in any observational channel — sightings,
  strandings, bycatch, fishery observers, OBIS, GBIF and iNaturalist. Where it has been recorded,
  however rarely, it keeps its v7 value: a down-weight shared across an ecoregion would cancel under
  the ecoregional rescale (@eq-ecoregion-rescale), and no weight can take a species out of a cell under
  the integer floor of 1.\n")
  if (on("right_whale_gulf_rule")) cat(
"- **Right whale Gulf rule** (`right_whale_gulf_rule = on`): the North Atlantic right whale is
  excluded from the two Gulf of America ecoregions, outside its range, where its v7 presence came
  only from the IUCN range polygon and AquaMaps [@roberts2016; @ward_geiger2011].\n")
  cat("\n")
  cat(glue::glue(
"The table applied is fingerprinted in the release as `zone_exclusions_hash = {g('zone_exclusions_hash')}`;
the rules as equations, the evidence per species, ecoregion and channel, and the cells each row
removes are in @sec-release-v7c. Turning both rules off reproduces v7's merged models exactly."))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

Because risk is already inside the merged values, turtles receive `er_score = 100` at scoring time as a pass-through multiplier (flagged `is_er_spatial`), which cancels in the division by 100 rather than double-counting.

### Step 5 — NMFS DPS-listed species: the model stays the distribution, risk varies by cell

A second group of species carries extinction risk that varies across the range without being sea turtles: those whose ESA *listed entity* is a Distinct Population Segment, an ESU or a subspecies rather than the whole species — the humpback whale, the Southern Resident killer whale, Cook Inlet beluga, the salmon and steelhead ESUs, both sturgeons, and the others listed under *NMFS Distinct Population Segments* in @sec-data-sources. For them the pipeline builds a per-cell extinction-risk surface (`dps_nmfs`): each listed entity's designated critical habitat at that entity's status, and the species' baseline everywhere else in its IUCN range (the MMPA floor of 20 for a marine mammal; the IUCN category otherwise).

These species do **not** use the turtle multiplication. Their merged value is the **distribution** — the suitability surface (AquaX, or AquaMaps where AquaX did not model the species) masked to the extinction-risk footprint, exactly the range mask every other taxon receives, with a cell that no suitability model covers valued at its risk, as in the plain rule — and the per-cell risk is carried **beside** the value rather than inside it:

$$
v_{c} = \begin{cases} v_{suit,c} & \text{where a suitability model covers } c \\ v_{er,c} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
\qquad\qquad er_{c} = v_{er,c}
$$ {#eq-merge-dps}

Scoring then multiplies the two (@sec-scoring), so the score is the same extinction-risk-weighted suitability the turtle rule produces — computed one step later. What changes is what the merged model *shows*: under the turtle rule the humpback, whose risk is the MMPA baseline across 99.8 % of its range, collapsed to a near-flat minimum everywhere outside critical habitat — the map drew the *weight*, not the whale. Now the merged model is the whale's habitat suitability, and its risk is a separate layer (*NMFS DPS extinction risk* in the species app).

Critical-habitat datasets are not an input for these species: `dps_nmfs` already carries every designation at its own entity's status, whereas the generic critical-habitat layers carry the species-level status (Endangered for the humpback) and would override the Threatened Mexico DPS habitat back to Endangered.

::: {.callout-note}
## Three merge strategies

- **Most taxa** — range-constrained maximum, then a **scalar** extinction-risk weight at scoring time.
- **Sea turtles** — an extinction-risk **raster** multiplied into the merged model, so risk varies spatially within the species.
- **NMFS DPS-listed species** — the merged model is the suitability; an extinction-risk **raster** is kept beside it and multiplied in at scoring time.
:::

## Where extinction risk enters

The governing `er_score` (@sec-extinction-risk) is applied **at merge time**, valuing the range cells — the point at which a species' presence in a cell should carry its governing risk rather than whatever code the contributing dataset happened to record. Applying it later, at scoring, would lose that: the merged surface would carry source-specific codes that may be stale or out of jurisdiction. The NMFS DPS-listed species are the deliberate exception: their risk is a per-cell surface built from the listings themselves, so it is carried beside the merged value and applied at scoring, where the per-cell weight replaces the scalar one.

## The statutory floors

The MMPA (20) and MBTA (10) floors are part of the governing `er_score`, not a separate pass over the cells. A marine mammal's range cells therefore carry at least 20 wherever it is present, and a CFR 50 §10.13 migratory bird at least 10 — see @sec-extinction-risk for how each flag is assigned, and why the MBTA one is a species list rather than "all birds".

## Persisted output

```{r}
#| label: merge-outputs
#| output: asis

idf <- doc_manifest()$id_field
cat("The merged result is stored as:\n\n",
"- **`model`** — one row per merged model, keyed by `", idf, "`.\n",
"- **`model_cell`** — one row per model × cell, holding the merged value in `val`.\n\n", sep = "")
if (mdl_key_style) {
  cat(
"`mdl_key` is a **stable** identifier of the form `{dataset}|{species}` — `am|Fis-29291`,
`ms_merge|WORMS:137209`. It replaced an auto-increment id that renumbered on every rebuild,
which broke every saved link to a model.\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

## Validity after merging

A taxon is flagged valid once merging has run, on the criteria in @sec-taxonomy — chiefly that it resolved to a taxon, is marine and not extinct, and has at least one merged cell in the study area. Program-Area overlap is **not** among them from v7 onward; it is a spatial question answered later.

```{r}
#| label: merge-counts
#| output: asis

cat("In ", doc_ver(), " this yields **", doc_stat("valid_species"),
    " valid species** across the study area", sep = "")
if (doc_can("programareas")) cat(", of which **", doc_stat("species_program_areas"),
    "** contribute to scores within the ", doc_stat("n_program_areas"),
    " BOEM Program Areas of the current program cycle", sep = "")
cat(".\n\n")
```

## Guarding the rules

Every merge category has a synthetic fixture in the `msens` test suite asserting its exact expected output: range-only, both-masked, range-outside-the-US excluded, AquaMaps-only single-model, AquaMaps-only multi-model (which must **not** deduplicate), and the multiplicative turtle case.

This is deliberate. Whole-pipeline checks — the version-equivalence gate on Program-Area scores, and the content-hash checkpoints — catch *aggregate* drift, but they hide rule-level breakage: the ~750 wrongly-included species above moved aggregate scores almost not at all while being scientifically wrong. A category with no fixture is a category that can break silently.
